theme: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

reports.title: Michael Huggon: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: We will put on educational sessions to update our clinicians on the mental capacity act, managing challenging scenarios with particular emphasis on how this is documented in a patient record
promises.summary: Educational sessions on mental capacity act documentation

concerns.quote: I was told at the hearing that it is now normal practice for any work unfinished by surgery closing time is left to the after hours service and that GPs no longer "call in on the way home
concerns.hazard: unfinished work left to after hours service

concerns.quote: Given the above I am concerned that future deaths may occur if urgent requests are not dealt with more promptly
It is not within my authority as a coroner to suggest what action might be taken but I would be happy to discuss this matter informally

reports.title: Thomas Mallinson: Prevention of Future Deaths Report
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

concerns.quote: I wish to thank [REDACTED] for his attendance and and assistance at the hearing. It was acknowledged that on 18th the advice
concerns.hazard: lack of face to face assessment for elderly patient with comorbidities

concerns.quote: Thomas's case was sent electronically to the service, marked for 2 hour attention
there was no alert to a call handler to indicate recent contacts for the same patient with the same condition
concerns.hazard: lack of continuity alert for repeated calls

concerns.quote: In my summing up after hearing the evidence in this case I explained the legal concept of neglect as a failure to provide basic care and (in this case) medical attention for someone in a dependent condition who can not provide it for himself

links.explanation: Both reports highlight that urgent requests or referrals are not being handled promptly, leading to avoidable harm. The earlier report focuses on delayed handover and after‑hours coverage, while the later report concerns an electronically flagged 2‑hour referral that was not acted on due to workload.
